label: conj:algebraic-geometric-dilog-equivalence
title: Algebraic-geometric dilogarithm equivalence: $\Phi_n(x; q)$ poles map to ideal-tetrahedron cusps
html:
Superseded. The scalar substrate density \rho_q = 1/\hbar_q^2 used below is the structurally-wrong leading-order ansatz; the operator-valued form supersedes it (mass-endomorphism-tower); the canonical replacement is the operator-valued A^\lambda_{\mu, \nu}(I) graded expansion prop:rho-k-graded-expansion.

Conjecture (Algebraic-geometric dilogarithm equivalence). The categorical Markov trace of the nonabelian multiplicative integral over a lifted transient crossing (mass identity) evaluates algebraically to a rational function in \mathbb{Z}[q^{1/2}, q^{-1/2}, x] governed by the q-Pochhammer partial product \Phi_n(x; q) = \prod_{k=0}^{n-1}(1 - x q^k)^{-1} (q-Pochhammer partial product). Under the Archimedean realization \tau_{\mathrm{arch}} (archimedean realization functor):

  1. (Pole-to-cusp bijection.) The roots \{x = q^{-k} : k = 0, \dots, n-1\} of the denominator (x; q)_n are in bijection with the n ideal tetrahedra of a hyperbolic triangulation of the \Phi_q-piece K_S of the lifted transient crossing (Φ_q-piece), the root of index k labelling the tetrahedron whose shape parameter it seeds.

  2. (Asymptotic Bloch–Wigner.) The asymptotic of the partial product under Faddeev's scaling (Archimedean limit) recovers the Bloch–Wigner dilogarithm D(z) at the matched shape parameter, so

  \tau_{\mathrm{arch}}\!\bigl(\Phi_n(x; q_0)\bigr)
  \;\xrightarrow[n \to \infty]{}\;
  D(z(x))
  \;=\;
  \mathrm{Vol}_{\mathrm{hyp}}\bigl(\Delta_{z(x)}\bigr),

where z(x) is the shape parameter of the ideal tetrahedron \Delta_{z(x)} that triangulates K_S.

  1. (Mass formula.) The \tau_{\mathrm{arch}}-image of the transient mass element is
  \tau_{\mathrm{arch}}\!\bigl(\mathfrak{m}^{\mathrm{trans}}(\varrho)\bigr)
  \;=\;
  \rho_q \cdot
  \!\!\sum_{S \subseteq \{0,\dots,n-2\}}\!\!
  D\bigl(z(\lvert V_S\rvert)\bigr)
  \;=\;
  \rho_q \cdot
  \mathrm{Vol}_{\mathrm{hyp}}(S^3 \setminus K),

recovering the JSJ piecewise sum used in the canonical binding- energy pipeline (cf. Φ_q-tower JSJ bridge).

Note — what n is, and it is not pinned. Clause (1) counts n ideal tetrahedra because that is what the carrier of the bijection (shared-denominator cusp holonomy, table row 4) and the compute both count: snappy_cusp_seeding.py takes n from num_tetrahedra() and emits one algebraic seed per tetrahedron, eight for the eight-tetrahedron \mathtt{L6a4}. But the same symbol is the Hecke index and GB-depth k_\star(T_w) = n in that carrier's own hypothesis, a free truncation order swept over 1, \dots, 4 in q-pochhammer-seed.witness.json, and unbounded in clause (2) below, which takes n \to \infty. For the figure-eight 4_1 these disagree: the triangulation has 2 tetrahedra and 1 cusp, while the braid whose closure it is has Hecke index 3. So clause (1) fixes the geometric object the roots label without fixing the count, and no clause here should be read as asserting that the Hecke depth equals the tetrahedron count — that identification is asserted in thurston-relaxation as the "GB-PL bijection" and is not established here.

Relation to the structural form of Kashaev

The conjecture is the QOU-native, partial-product form of the Kashaev–Murakami–Murakami theorem (Kashaev volume conjecture). Kashaev–MM pass through the colored Jones polynomial at roots of unity; the present conjecture passes through the explicit shared denominator:

Side Object Pole / singularity
Algebraic (R) \Phi_n(x; q_0) zero of (1 - x q^k) at x = q^{-k}
Archimedean (\mathbb{C}) \mathrm{Li}_2 logarithmic singularity at t = 1
Geometric (\mathbf{Hyp}_3) ideal tetrahedron \Delta_{z_k} complete cusp of \Delta_{z_k}

The bijection between the rows is the content of (shared-denominator cusp holonomy). Under that bijection, the algebraic state sum and the hyperbolic volume are the same regulator \Phi_n(x; q_0) \mapsto D(z(x)) evaluated through two convergence schemes.

Conjectural standing

This result is downstream of (Kashaev volume conjecture) and (Archimedean limit), so it is necessarily a conjecture — propagation of conjectural backing forbids promotion to proposition/theorem.

The Lean formalization follows the hypothesis-carrying conditional-class pattern: the class QOU.QPochhammer.AlgebraicGeometricEquivalence carries the open inputs — the matched shape parameter z(x), the volume-conjecture saddle asymptotic (a theorem for 4_1 by Ohtsuki / Andersen–Hansen), and the matched-cusp volume identification supplied by (shared-denominator cusp holonomy) — and the statement bundle QOU.QPochhammer.algebraic_geometric_equivalence derives both halves: item 1 (pole side) unconditionally, as the sorry-free theorem denomPolyLocal_roots_explicit (each x = q^{-k} is a genuine root of (x;q)_n), and item 2 (Bloch–Wigner asymptotic) from the class fields. The class asserts nothing provable-outright; no instance is fabricated. This matches the conjectural-class pattern used for Φ_q-tower JSJ bridge.

The shape parameter is a field, on the upper half plane. Item 2 above states the asymptotic at D(z(x)), with z(x) the shape of the ideal tetrahedron; an earlier Lean revision typed the Bloch–Wigner function D \colon \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R} and applied it to the state variable x itself, on the grounds that the matching map had been composed away. That diverged from the statement above, and it was not a harmless simplification: D is conjugation-antisymmetric, D(\bar z) = -D(z), so D vanishes identically on the reals and every volume the class could name was forced to zero — a flat tetrahedron, which is the negation of the conjecture rather than a weak form of it. The map is now un-composed: shape is a class field typed UpperHalfPlane, so a degenerate shape is not expressible, and x keeps its own role as the q-Pochhammer state variable. The sibling (shared-denominator cusp holonomy) had already made the same repair on its own shape assignment.

The bar-odd open item: argument identification to S

The equivalence above is the bar-even face of the correspondence: the asymptotic recovers the real volume D(z) = \mathrm{Vol}_{\mathrm{hyp}}, which for the amphichiral 4_1 supplies the -\mathrm{Vol}(4_1) part of the Q_\beta coefficient c_3. Its bar-odd companion is the anchor-dependent leak S = c_3 + \mathrm{Vol}(4_1), carried not by the compact \Phi_q but by the Faddeev non-compact \Phi_b (modular double). The open item is the argument-identification map: the structural map q_0 \mapsto z(q_0) — the substrate-to-meridian-holonomy map supplied by the same pole-to-cusp matching as items 1–2 — such that the fibre-branch Faddeev phase at the identified argument reproduces S:

  \arg \Phi_{b(q_0)}\bigl(z(q_0)\bigr) \;=\; S(q_0),
  \qquad
  b(q_0) \;=\; \sqrt{\tfrac{\ln q_0}{2\pi}}.

The Lean carrier is the hypothesis class QOU.QBeta.PhiBSArgumentIdentification.SArgumentIdentification, parametrized by the argument map itself: a bare existence claim (\forall q_0\, \exists z) would be near-vacuous by pointwise choice against the unbounded continuous phase, so the class carries the structural map as a parameter and no instance is fabricated. Two consequences are derived unconditionally from the class:

  1. (Unimodular readout.) At the identified argument the \Phi_b value is the pure phase e^{i S(q_0)} — the leak is the argument of a \sigma-unitary (unitary phases are bar-odd).

  2. (Zero crossing — conditional on a sign flip the data does not establish.) If S changes sign between the anchors, continuity of S on q_0 > 1 forces by the intermediate value theorem a substrate q^{*} where S(q^{*}) = 0: there c_3 = -\mathrm{Vol}(4_1) and the \Phi_b readout is 1 (Lean: exists_zero_crossing, exists_pure_bar_even, which take the flip as an explicit hypothesis). The premise is not established by the data: each anchor value S(\text{muon}) \approx +0.00968, S(\text{proton}) \approx -0.03946 carries a CAL-3 propagated uncertainty of \pm 1.26 (130× / 32× the value); only the swing S(\text{muon}) - S(\text{proton}) is resolved, and it is the cross-anchor c_3 difference with \mathrm{Vol}(4_1) cancelled. So the zero-crossing is a conditional structural statement, not an established prediction. (The onward identification of this S-channel with the resurgent monodromy datum A_\omega has no literature support and is not derivable; recorded in docs/audits/2026-08-14-aomega-to-S-bridge-refuted-O2-negative.md.)

The fibre branch (\lvert q \rvert = 1, real b) and construction status

The physical regime of the bar-odd face is the fibre branch: real b, where the modular parameter q_b = e^{i\pi b^2} satisfies \lvert q_b \rvert = 1 and equals the pure phase e^{i \ln q_0 / 2} at the substrate map (Lean: norm_fibreQParam, fibreQParam_fibreB). On this branch the modular-double product diverges and the construction is the real single integral phiB (QOU.MathlibExt.FaddeevPhiBRealIntegral), whose structural laws — self-duality \Phi_{b^{-1}} = \Phi_b, unitarity \lvert \Phi_b \rvert = 1, the inversion relation, and \sigma-unitarity \Phi_b \cdot \overline{\Phi_b} = 1 — hold for the defined object unconditionally. By the rigidity clause of (unitary phases are bar-odd), the fibre-branch \Phi_b is an intrinsically bar-odd carrier.

Of the two analytic identifications behind the construction, the integrability of the Faddeev kernel is now a fully unconditional theorem: the near-0 piece (integrableOn_kernel_Ioc_zero_one — the -2z/t^2 subtraction cancels the pole, via the two-sided cubic \sinh estimates and a global \lvert \sin y - y \rvert \le 2\lvert y \rvert^3 bound), the exponential-domination tail on [1, \infty) (integrableOn_kernel_Ioi_one), and hence integrability on all of (0, \infty) (integrableOn_kernel_Ioi_zero) are all hypothesis-free — the two standard majorant facts (e^{-bt} and t^{-2} integrable on [1, \infty)) are discharged from Mathlib, not carried. The definition-to-contour identity — that the real-integral phiB equals the Faddeev contour integral — remains a numerical pin (8 \times 10^{-29} against the validated contour evaluator) and is assumed nowhere in the Lean; its honest carrier is QOU.MathlibExt.PhiBFibreExtension (the constructed phiB extends to a full Faddeev \Phi_b; no instance).

Binding channel: conditional only

The identification of the bar-odd face with the decay observable \mathfrak{Q}_\beta = \mathrm{Im}\,\mathfrak{V} — and with it any "decay equals binding" reading of the Gram-ghost mode — is conditional on the complex-volume unification (binding–Q_\beta complex volume). \Phi_b touches binding only through that unproven channel identity; no statement here or in the Lean carriers above assumes it. The channel is carried explicitly as the class SDeformedVolumeChannel (u(q_0) map + deformed volume + the identity S = \mathrm{Im}\,\mathfrak{V}(u(q_0))), and the composition with the argument-identification map is derived, not assumed: phase_eq_im_deformed_volume, phiB_eq_cs_phase, and exists_cs_vanishing (the sign flip of S forces a substrate point with vanishing deformed Chern–Simons part).

Witness

Two witnesses bracket the matching, and neither is a SnapPy cusp solve driven from the algebraic seeds.

q-pochhammer-seed.witness.json sweeps the partial-product order over n = 1, \dots, 4; at each order it extracts the n denominator zeros q_0^{-k}, lifts them off the real line by a fixed imaginary perturbation, and drives Newton-Raphson from each seed onto the colour-tube discriminant \Delta(z) = 0 — not onto the Thurston gluing equations. Nine of its ten runs converge, in at most 11 iterations. Its own caveat records that it "does not yet drive a SnapPy Newton iteration".

snappy-cusp-seeding.witness.json is the SnapPy side. It compares the bare algebraic seeds against SnapPy's converged tetrahedral shape parameters for the figure-eight 4_1 (\mathtt{m004}), its sister \mathtt{m003}, and the Borromean rings \mathtt{L6a4}, and reports the pairing distance; it seeds no solve. Those distances (0.40 to 0.91) are what bound the conjecture's canonical form, as shared-denominator cusp holonomy §Empirical scope records.
